warnings: This study focuses on Zn-biofortified SEEDS effects, not direct Zn fertilizer application
Only soil Zn fertilization treatment (50 kg ZnSO4·7H2O ha⁻¹) matches meta-analysis intervention
High-Zn seeds are NOT the same as Zn fertilizer application - they are biofortified seeds from previous crops
Multiple crops, countries, and years create complex experimental structure
Some locations show non-significant differences (marked NS)
Different varieties used across locations could confound results
Grain Zn concentration data has high variability across locations and years

recon.control_definition: Local control treatment (i.e., basal N,P,K fertilizers only, no Zn application), using low-Zn seeds
recon.treatment_definition: Local control treatment plus soil Zn application of 50kg ZnSO4·7H2O ha⁻¹, using low-Zn seeds
recon.potential_tc_confusion: High-Zn seeds treatment exists but is NOT Zn fertilizer application - it's biofortified seeds
recon.sample_size_source: All field experiments were laid out in randomized complete block design with four replications for wheat and rice and six replications for common bean
recon.extraction_guidance: Extract only soil Zn fertilization vs control comparisons from Tables 8 and 9. Ignore high-Zn seed treatments as they represent biofortified seeds, not Zn fertilizer application. Extract data separately by location, year, and crop species. Use LSD values as variance measure. Note that some comparisons show NS (non-significant) results.
